nar.text: Just before 3 PM the nine contestants paraded on to the track towards the starting line to position the cars in two rows, according to lots drawn.
The final was started at 3:00 PM when Varzi took the lead.
After the first lap, as they passed the grandstands in close order, the first 5 cars flew by within less than three seconds: Varzi, Borzacchini, Maserati, Arcangeli and Nuvolari.
Alfieri Maserati drives his 16-cylinder into the lead with a 1m21s lap; Brilli Peri passes Nuvolari for fifth.
Brilli Peri passed Arcangeli to gain fourth place.
After lap four, Alfieri Maserati headed the leading pack by 3.6 seconds to Varzi, 5.4s to Borzacchini and 5.6s to Brilli Peri.
Maserati's lead is down to 2.8s; Brilli Peri passes Borzacchini for third, and Ruggeri is lapped.
On the sixth lap, Varzi closed up on the leading Maserati and was less than a second behind. The order of the following cars remained the same, except Momberger passed Caflisch.

On lap eight, Maserati was still in the lead, ahead of Varzi, Brilli Peri and Borzacchini, who had a tire throw a thread at the left front wheel in front of the grandstand and slowed to reach his pit.

During the ninth lap, Maserati led Varzi by 1.6s, while Brilli Peri lost 32 seconds as a result of the thrown tread which forced him to slow down. Borzacchini spent a lot of time at his pit to change a wheel, falling to last position, two laps behind.
On lap ten, Maserati led Varzi by 1.2s, while Brilli Peri lost over one minute in the pits to change the wheel and fell back four places.
Varzi takes the lead as Alfieri Maserati heads for the pits.
During lap 12, Alfieri Maserati fell to seventh place while he was at his pit replacing several spark plugs that had failed.
Only Arcangeli and Nuvolari were on the same lap with Varzi, all others were lapped at least once, Borzacchini and Ruggeri twice.
At the end of lap 13, the positions had not changed. Varzi was 43 seconds ahead of Arcangeli and 1m5.2s of Nuvolari.
On lap 14, there was only one change when Momberger passed Caflisch. The two Mercedes drivers provided good entertainment.
On lap 16, Caflisch passed Momberger and the 16-cylinder Maserati came chasing from behind.
Varzi leads Arcangeli by 52.6s; Alfieri Maserati passes both Mercedes for fifth.
Arcangeli, who had held second place since lap 12, began to slow down with ignition problems.
Varzi laps Nuvolari, now second, with Brilli Peri two seconds behind Nuvolari; Arcangeli drops from second to seventh.
Brilli Peri did not pass Nuvolari as expected, instead he slowed down with a loose exhaust.
Arcangeli retired the Talbot with a broken ignition wire.
At the end of lap 22, the last lap, Varzi finished first which amounted to a very Italian victory
Nuvolari is second, over a minute ahead of Momberger; Brilli Peri stops to remove his loose exhaust and falls to fourth.
